The Ecology of the Wayward Beasts
Nomadic Ascension
The spider may not be the largest, nor the most deadly of 
creatures that roam throughout the island. But when those eight 
articulated legs speed across the Farplains, leap from coral 
outcroppings on the Strands or scurry around tree trunks in the 
Wealdwoods, many creatures fear for their very lives. With a 
sharp blade-like edge running along the top of its abdomen, it 
has been known to rush under larger megafauna, slitting their 
stomachs from below, in a ghastly display of brutality
One of the very few corals that ever move

as it is carried far and wide. Ranging from

Sunlight, like a breath of fresh air, revitalizes the Traveler as they step out from the Umbrawells crevice and into the cold of the Splitspine mountain cliff 
top. With eyes closed, the Traveler savors the feeling of the wind pulling at their hair and tattered clothing, torn and singed from the acidic environment 
below. Breathing out a sigh of relief at surviving such a trial, they open their eyes and are rewarded with a view that suddenly feels worth the struggle. 
Under sparsely clouded skies, the Traveler can see farther than they ever have since stepping onto the island. Miles of Wealdwoods spread out to the east, 
waves of green leaves rolling over unseen hills. Past the last tree, a vibrant riot of color encroaches on the coast, distant waves break on the Strands and 
even from the great distance, the Traveler can see the white specks of birds swirl about the teeming hordes of crustacean.
Sitting on the stone ground, the Traveler pulls hardtack and their journal from their pack, and begins to write and sketch of their journey down below: 
exotic mushrooms that lit the caverns, the skittering monstrosities that called it home and speculation notes on what was in the center of the webbed lair. 
As the sun sinks lower in the sky, a large body suddenly thumps onto the ground behind them. With journal clutched tightly to their chest,  they quickly 
spin about to find golden eyes peering at them from a large canine-like head. Staying perfectly still, the Traveler and their sudden visitor stare cautiously 
at each other for a few moments, before the winged beast slowly approaches on clawed wings. With its large, furred head near the Traveler's chest, the 
winged beast sniffs the biped. Then, with an uneasy smirk, the Traveler calmly offers the hardtack.
With a quick snap of its long snout, the mammal snatches the biscuit from their hand, and crunches happily. Taking a risk, one the Traveler would have 
never expected this island to allow, reaches out  and runs their fingers through the warm ruddy fur of the skyelarx's neck.
  
"Maybe I don't need to do this all alone..." 
For a species to survive and thrive, it means carving a niche of its own, a clear space in the web of life. While true for the vast majority of 
animals that have swam, flew and crawled across Sol'Kesh, they are not as likely to survive an ecological upheaval as well as a creature 
that can adapt to any environment it finds itself in. This rare trait of evolution, often only bestowed upon the most basal of insects or 
most indiscriminate of scavengers, allows highly versatile creatures to flourish everywhere.
Many wayward creatures roam across vast landscapes. Nicalliath, sacrissian and skyelarx never spend more than a night in a single 
area, forever on the move for fresher hunting grounds. For while they are ferocious predators in their own right, they are never fully 
suited to the environment's ecology, and there is always a greater predator, often an apex that would oust them from their territory.
Others simply adapt so successfully to any niche, that they are found nearly everywhere: swarms of lanceleth squeeze under every rock 
and branch, lethally leaping into whatever unfortunate beast steps near, packs of social vinnirex hunt across fields and beaches with 
ease, wrakis crawl into any crevice they can find, and scavick plague and pester every biome. These festering rodents making up the 
most commonly found scavenger, as well as prey.
Lastly, the omaterssum, wandering far across the island not out of significant adaptability, but out of desperation. With a dwindling 
rate of reproduction, the large marsupial escapes predation wherever it can, whether that be an uninhabited spire of rock off the coast, 
or a dark crevice in the side of a cliff. Trying to secure a last niche of their own anywhere, before it's too late.
